Two vectors may be multiplied to give a scalar. The symbol \boldsymbol{\cdot} is used to denote this kind of multiplication. The scalar product of vectors \underline{\mathbf{a}} and \underline{\mathbf{b}} is written as \underline{\mathbf{a}}\boldsymbol{\cdot}\underline{\mathbf{b}}. It is often pronounced as \underline{\mathbf{a}} ‘dot’ \underline{\mathbf{b}} and is sometimes also referred to as the “dot product”. As the name suggests, the result of the scalar product is a scalar. Given two vectors, \underline{\mathbf{a}} and \underline{\mathbf{b}} , the scalar product \underline{\mathbf{a}}\boldsymbol{\cdot}\underline{\mathbf{b}} is defined as equation (4.3.1) (4.3.1) \underline{\mathbf{a}}\boldsymbol{\cdot}\underline{\mathbf{b}}=\lvert% \underline{\mathbf{a}}\rvert\lvert\underline{\mathbf{b}}\rvert\cos\theta, where \theta is the angle between the vectors.
